source.rationale: Permanent eval-level regression case for the exact scenario Engineering Decision Log Entry 21 verified by hand (80 raw points for a favorable embedding-sourced link vs. 45 for an unfavorable heuristic-sourced link) -- that check currently only exists as a unit-level rubric test, not an end-to-end eval case. Constructed so the embedding-sourced link has a favorable change_type (pure addition) and tight blast radius (single short doc section), which would out-score a real but weaker heuristic link on raw points alone, to confirm the TIER cap (not point arithmetic) is what actually prevents 'High' here.

stale_doc_section:
Log lines are written to the sink but are not flushed automatically after
each message; call `.flush()` manually if you need durability guarantees
before the process exits.

labels.notes_for_labeler: CONFIRMED (real run) for verifier/corrector -- clean, accurate proposed correction. REAL BUG FOUND, NOT just an eval gap: validator_status came back as error_unvalidated with 'Validator response could not be parsed: Unterminated string starting at: line 3 column 16 (char 50)'. This is a JSON-parsing failure in validator.py's handling of the LLM's structured output, not a content problem with this case. Notably, case 019 (default_value_change_boolean_flip) hit the EXACT same error text at the EXACT same character offset (char 50) in the same run -- strongly suggests a systematic issue (e.g. an unescaped newline or quote inside a multi-line validator_rationale breaking JSON string parsing) rather than two independent flukes. validator_status left unscored pending a fix to validator.py's response parsing and a rerun. RECOMMEND treating this as a priority Engineering Decision Log item -- a validator that can silently fail to parse its own LLM's output on ordinary (not adversarial) content is a real production risk, separate from and more urgent than any eval-dataset-authoring question.
